title: Prior and future summer ozone slopes did not clearly differ in four US bird richness samples in 1995-2023
abstract: We tested whether recorded bird richness had a different slope for prior and future summer ozone. We reused a verified public-data panel and matched May-September ozone windows by exact route and year. Four US region and period samples in 1995-2023 had 26,868 surveys. Models controlled current ozone, seasonal weather, survey conditions, route, observer and region-year effects. Prior-minus-future slopes were +0.092, -0.237, -0.198 and -0.446 species per 10 ppb. All four 98.75 percent state-cluster intervals included zero. All trend, observer and distance checks also included zero. A separate dense calculation checked one model. The result does not establish equal slopes or no ecological effect. Future survey coverage selects routes. Coarse exposure, detection bias, few western states and cross-state dependence limit inference. This is a time-order audit of shared observations, not a new causal estimate or an independent source-data replication.

display.caption: Prior minus future May-September ozone slopes. Bars show 98.75 percent state-cluster intervals for four separate tests. All intervals include zero.

citations.reason: We reuse its unchanged panel and four raw-build scripts with attribution. We add matched-season future exposure and a direct prior-minus-future contrast. Source observations overlap.
Its uncertainty audit motivates caution about cross-state annual errors. We do not reuse its fitted models.
